rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice before an adjective or verb to mean sufficiently, as in 夠熟 or 夠食.

example.english: This portion of rice is enough to eat.
example.jyutping: ni1 fan6 faan6 gau3 sik6 laa3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday way to say that the amount is sufficient, including when the thing being counted is understood.

example.english: That's enough; we don't need to buy any more.
example.jyutping: gau3 laa3 m4 sai2 zoi3 maai5

rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken pattern when the noun is something being consumed, used, or obtained in a sufficient amount.
Use this colloquial pattern with resource nouns such as 錢, 時間, and 位 when saying that there is enough of something.

example.english: We have enough money to take a taxi home.
example.traditional: 我哋夠錢搭的士返屋企。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 gau3 cin4 daap3 dik1 si2 faan1 uk1 kei2

rows.note: Choose this more general attributive pattern when enough quantity is being described before an ordinary noun rather than expressed through a verb.

example.traditional: 呢個計劃有足夠嘅資源。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 gai3 waak6 jau5 zuk1 gau3 ge3 zi1 jyun4
